The page loads and renders correctly for about one second, then an obfuscated inline script on highgardenroses.com itself sets document.head.innerHTML and document.body.innerHTML to empty and starts an eval('debugger;') loop. The script decides by timing console calls, which is a standard way of detecting an open developer-tools or automation connection. This is the seller's own anti-automation measure, not a network block: the HTML arrives in full (586 KB) and cdn.shopify.com is now reachable. No attempt was made to defeat the detection, per the standing rule against bypassing website access controls. The listing remains verifiable through the site's public product feed, which is how this case is re-verified each run.
